CHUNKING

Size & overlap

Retrieval can only return what a chunk contains. So how you cut the document decides what's even

findable.
CHUNK SIZE Too large buries the answer among unrelated text and weakens the match. Too small strips away the context a passage
needs to make sense.
OVERLAP Repeat a little text between neighbours so an idea split across a boundary still lands whole in at least one chunk. ©
NO DEFAULT The right values depend on your documents. You pick, you test, you adjust — never copy a number blind.

Cosine compares direction (meaning); dot product also rewards magnitude. They can rank results differently — match
the metric to your model.

The embedding model decides where meaning lands. A better one separates text that looks similar but means different
things.

APPROXIMATE SEARCH
